proposal.title: Azure sensor anomaly detection: first end-to-end sketch
proposal.body: Scope: synthetic sensor events → Event Hubs (ingest and durable buffer) → Functions validator (schema, units; invalid events go to Blob quarantine) → Azure ML online endpoint (anomaly score) → Cosmos DB results → Azure Monitor alert → operator. Assumptions: region and subscription aren't chosen, the model isn't selected or validated, and local tests use a scripted model reply. Azure isn't covered by native Terraform here, so these components need engineering work. The diagram doesn't prove deployment or connectivity.

data.label: Synthetic device simulator
data.description: Existing test source that sends JSON events {deviceId, timestamp, value, unit}. Outside the provisioning scope.

data.label: Event ingestion & buffer
data.description: Receives events and holds them durably for a retention window that is still to be agreed. Partitions by deviceId to keep per-device order. Consumers use checkpoints so processing can be replayed.

data.label: Validation function
data.description: Event Hubs-triggered function. Checks the schema, the required deviceId, timestamp and unit, and the allowed units. Passes the original fields through unchanged.

data.label: Invalid event quarantine
data.description: Private container that stores rejected events with the rejection reason, for review and replay.

data.label: Anomaly scoring endpoint
data.description: Returns an anomaly score per event. The model isn't chosen yet. Local tests use a scripted reply, which does not validate model quality.
data.service: Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint

data.label: Anomaly results store
data.description: Stores the score with deviceId, timestamp, unit and model version. Uses deviceId as the partition key. Writes are idempotent per event ID.

data.label: Operator alerting
data.description: Raises an alert when a score is at or above the agreed threshold. The threshold and the notification channel are still to be agreed.

data.label: Operator
data.description: Person who receives and handles anomaly alerts.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If identity or units are lost, anomaly results can't be traced or trusted, and mixed units can cause false alarms.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Preserve device identity, timestamps and units."
requirementDrafts.statement: Every event keeps its device ID, event timestamp and measurement unit unchanged from intake through to results and alerts. Events missing any of these are rejected to quarantine with a reason.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without a buffer, an outage in validation or inference loses events. The retention period still needs to be agreed.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: accepted events stay buffered durably so processing can resume or replay after a downstream failure without losing data.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Too many false alarms make operators ignore alerts. The threshold and acceptable false-alarm rate are still open.
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the operator gets an alert for each anomaly at or above the agreed score threshold, including device ID, timestamp and score. Repeated alerts for the same device are suppressed.

Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with the exact evidence state. If blocked before checks, explicitly say runtime tests have not run and the design is not yet validated. An empty failures list NEVER means a sound, complete or correct design. Celebrate only named checks that actually passed. Explain the most important remaining issue in plain language and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message:
No runtime tests ran (0 checks), so I can't validate any part of this design yet. All 8 components are blocked because there's no supported generator for Event Hubs, Functions, Azure ML, Cosmos DB or Monitor in this flow. That's product engineering work, not a mistake in your design, and the fix isn't to shrink the app down to just storage.

The quarantine Blob container looks like it fits the private-object-storage contract, but it's only half wired. To use that contract, we'd need an identity that can write to and read from the container. Do you want the validation function to write rejected events there, or should an existing operator identity read and replay them? Your answer decides which access contract we draw.
